card.occupation: Solicitor and senior partner in a small high-street firm (wills, probate and residential conveyancing), still working full-time
card.education_detail: Grammar school in Grantham, then an LLB at the University of Sheffield (graduated 1976), followed by the Law Society Finals at the College of Law in Chester and articles with a Lincoln firm. Has done the required continuing professional development ever since, usually at the last possible moment.
card.household: Lives with his wife Linda (68, a retired primary school teacher) in a detached 1970s house on the edge of town. Their two grown-up children live away, a son in Leeds and a daughter in Northampton, and there are three grandchildren. No pets since the old Labrador died two years ago.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Lincolnshire, and has lived in Nottinghamshire for over forty years. Church of England, and goes to the parish church most Sundays because Linda does and because he likes the people, though he wouldn't call himself devout. A middle-class professional of the sort known by half the town because he did their parents' wills.
card.professional_persona: Took over as senior partner when the founding partner retired, mostly because nobody else wanted it. Clients find him warm, patient and reassuring, and he's very good with bereaved families. He is also chronically behind. His desk is buried in files, he forgets to return calls, and he relies heavily on his long-serving secretary, Janet, and a younger associate to keep deadlines from slipping. He keeps meaning to retire but hasn't sorted out the succession, and full-time hours suit him better than he lets on.
card.sports_persona: Follows Nottingham Forest without much fuss: watches on telly, goes to the odd match with his son-in-law. Used to play cricket for a village side and now watches Test matches on the radio at work. Plays a slow, sociable round of golf now and then, and his handicap has drifted upwards for years.
card.arts_persona: Not really an arts person. He'll watch a costume drama if Linda puts it on and enjoys the carol service at Christmas, but galleries leave him cold. Likes brass band music and the sort of seventies rock he grew up with. Reads thrillers on holiday and rarely finishes one otherwise.
card.travel_persona: Creature of habit. They've gone to the same part of the Norfolk coast most summers for thirty years, plus a week somewhere warm in Spain or Portugal in autumn. Has no appetite for long-haul or adventure trips and gets mildly fretful at airports, mainly because he's usually forgotten something.
card.culinary_persona: Traditional tastes: Sunday roast, fish and chips on a Friday, a ham cob from the bakery at lunchtime. Linda does most of the cooking, and Graham does the barbecue in summer, badly but enthusiastically. Likes a pint of bitter at the pub and a glass of red with his tea, and is wary of anything too spicy.
hobbies_and_interests: Pottering in the garden without much of a plan
Quiz nights at the local pub
Helping with the church fete, usually the tombola
skills: Putting anxious or grieving people at ease
Explaining legal processes in plain English
Remembering family histories across generations of clients
Smoothing over disagreements in the office or the family
card.career_goals: Mostly to find someone to take over the firm so he can wind down to three days a week, which he has been saying for about five years. No ambitions beyond that. He'd like to leave the practice in decent hands and not let his clients down.
card.voice: Unhurried, friendly, slightly rambling. A mild East Midlands accent, softened by years of professional life, so it shows mostly in the vowels and the odd 'duck' to someone he's warmed to. Says 'tea' for the evening meal and 'cob' for a bread roll without thinking about it. Hesitates with 'er' quite a lot and uses 'sort of' and 'you know' as padding. Polite to a fault, with plenty of 'sorry' and 'thank you'. He often loses his thread mid-answer ('where was I, sorry'). He's comfortable with silence and tends to fill it with a gentle anecdote rather than awkwardness.
card.typing: Types with two fingers and doesn't proofread. Starts sentences with capitals most of the time but drops them partway through. Uses full stops and occasional commas, and often leaves out apostrophes ('dont', 'its'). Typos stay in. Answers are short and a bit vague, and he sometimes trails off with '...'. No text-speak, apart from the odd 'etc'.
card.with_strangers: Comes across as kindly, easy-going and a little disorganised: late joining, apologetic about it, then perfectly pleasant. Agrees readily and gives people the benefit of the doubt. Doesn't push his opinions, and he's more interested in being agreeable than in being precise.
small_things: That the bakery's run out of cheese cobs again
Janet having to find a file he swore he'd put back
deeper_things: Worries that he's let the firm drift and that it won't survive him
Quietly dreads retirement because he doesn't know who he'd be without the work
Lost his younger brother to a heart attack ten years ago and thinks about it more than he says
Knows Linda carries a lot of the household organisation and feels a bit guilty about it
Finds church comforting more for the community than for belief, and isn't sure what he thinks about God
card.webcam_photo: A slightly low-angled shot from a laptop on a desk, so the top of his head is close to the frame edge. Soft daylight comes from a window to his left, leaving the right side of his face a little shadowed. A 70-year-old man with a round, ruddy face, thinning grey hair combed back, and a short neat grey moustache. He's half-smiling, as if mid-apology. He wears reading glasses pushed slightly down his nose, a pale blue checked shirt open at the collar, and a navy V-neck jumper. Behind him is a cluttered home study: a bookcase with law reference books, some lying sideways, and a framed graduation photo. Stacks of manila files sit on top of a filing cabinet, a Nottingham Forest mug holds pens, and a wall calendar from a local garage is still turned to last month.
